topic: Punjabi number-word spelling for actual source written-number exercises

primary_readable_source.title: Wiktionary Western Punjabi number-data module
primary_readable_source.format: Born-digital readable HTML; table and displayed source data, not an OCR claim.
primary_readable_source.limits: Community lexical data with regional/orthographic variants, not specialist or native-speaker certification. Linked stand-alone entries for several queried words were redlinks, so they are not claimed as independent corroboration. No large-number lakh/crore notation is imported into the canonical source scale.

additional_html_inspection.title: Bashir and Kazmi, Punjabi-English Dictionary (2012), University of Chicago DSAL HTML search
additional_html_inspection.actual_use: The exact sixty-seven query returned no result. Broader searches displayed prose examples rather than resolving all requested numerals. The readable نیڑے entry (page592) supports ordinary near/nearly wording, not a certified rounding term. Truncated later broad output is not claimed fully read.
additional_html_inspection.excluded_pdf: The frontmatter link resolved to a35pagePDF. Its auto-extracted text was encountered but was not OCR/visually verified; it is not admitted here as usable number-word authority. No PDF was downloaded or relied on for the selected spellings.

use_limit: The existing12locus Rvel starter remains unchanged. This is a small topic-driven observation, not a new full-corpus snapshot, not a replacement for stage consultations, and not evidence that all Punjabi numeral variants are standardized.
